description: Contradicts ARC_TEMPLATES on purpose, mirroring datacenter_v1_world_b's structure for saas_premium's (currently generic) vocabulary. ARC_TEMPLATES.silent_churn/exec_sponsor_change assume disengagement is DOWNSTREAM of a relationship-event trigger and route every chain through a decision step before any outcome; this world reverses that direction on one edge and adds a real risk-to-expansion edge no template models.

dag.note: REVERSED vs ARC_TEMPLATES.silent_churn's assumed direction (engagement decline precedes usage decline). Here reduced usage precedes and drives the engagement drop, not the other way around -- a product-led-decline story, not a relationship-led one.

REAL EDGE NO TEMPLATE CONTAINS. An unhappy customer's team sometimes seeks a different (cheaper/better-fit) package from the same vendor rather than leaving outright -- a dissatisfaction-to-upsell-inquiry link no ARC_TEMPLATES arc models (all templates route dissatisfaction only toward at-risk/lost outcomes).

template_disagreements.template_edge: engagement decline precedes usage decline (relationship-led disengagement)
template_disagreements.this_world: usage_decline -> engagement_drop (product-led: reduced usage drives the engagement drop)

template_disagreements.template: (none -- no ARC_TEMPLATES arc connects dissatisfaction to an upsell/expansion signal)

template_disagreements.template_edge: NPS decline treated as part of the same disengagement chain as engagement/usage decline
template_disagreements.this_world: no edge between these two types in this world's true DAG -- see no_relationship absence below

absences.note: Real and admitted at this world's window (30d) -- boundary-case control, mirrors world_b's own note. See eval_profile/event_engine.py for the actual admission check.
